templates.name: Addition/similarity: a further item of the same kind
Contrast: established view or appearance, then a finding that breaks it
Contrast: positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence
Cause/effect: need or judgment, then the action it motivates
Concession: grant, then the main claim resumes (but / Still)
Concession: supported claim, then a fact that qualifies it
Emphasis: stronger same-direction fact (content-contrast trap at hard)
Specification/restatement: exact content or plain rewording
Sequence/time: next step, earlier or later event, end of a long effort
Culmination, alternative and place (ultimately, alternatively, there)
Example: general claim, then one named instance

items.passage: For a thousand years, most Icelandic farmhouses were built from blocks of turf stacked around wooden frames. Historians consider the design remarkably well suited to the island. ______ turf walls decayed within a few decades and had to be rebuilt, but sod was plentiful on an island with few trees, and its thick layers insulated interiors against subarctic winters.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence claims that the turf house design was “remarkably well suited to the island.” The blank sentence first admits a drawback that seems to cut against that claim (turf walls “decayed within a few decades and had to be rebuilt”) and then, with “but,” returns to the reasons the design suited Iceland. “Of course” fits: it introduces a point the writer grants before turning back to the main claim.

A.why_wrong: The design being well suited to Iceland does not lead to the walls decaying; the decay is a point against that claim, which is why the sentence goes on with “but.”

B.why_wrong: Walls that “decayed within a few decades” do not reword the claim that the design suited the island; they raise a problem with it.

D.why_wrong: “Additionally” would offer the decay as one more reason the design suited Iceland, but it is a drawback the writer concedes before the turn with “but.”

items.notes: Grant then turn inside one sentence: the concession, then “but” resumes the claim (3.17 shape; b1 used the Still shape). K1 has no band-7 official items (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md section 5), so band_target is 6. Trap: Additionally, for a reader who files the blank sentence as more description of the houses. No In fact, Indeed or Actually beside the concession key; no contrast decoy. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

band7.why: K1_grant_turn has no band-7 official items, so it cannot be band 7; it matches the band-6 Of course ... but shape of 974b5a8c, with a dense-enough grant and an additive decoy that pulls a reader who files the blank sentence as more description. A strong band 6.

items.passage: Glottochronology estimates when related languages separated by counting how much basic vocabulary they still share. Because it needs no written records, the method has been applied to language families whose early histories are otherwise unknown. ______ it assumes that basic words are replaced at a steady rate, and comparisons of languages with long written histories show that the rate varies considerably.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text first presents glottochronology as useful: because it “needs no written records,” it has been applied to language families “whose early histories are otherwise unknown.” The blank sentence then qualifies that usefulness: the method “assumes that basic words are replaced at a steady rate,” yet comparisons of well-recorded languages “show that the rate varies considerably.” “That said” fits, since it introduces a limitation that weakens the earlier point without denying it.

A.why_wrong: The method’s usefulness for families with no written records does not cause words to be replaced at uneven rates; the uneven rates are a problem for the method.

B.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not narrow the point about where the technique has been applied; it raises a weakness in the method’s basic assumption.

C.why_wrong: “Furthermore” would add the sentence as one more point in the method’s favor, but the finding “that the rate varies considerably” cuts against it.

items.notes: Band-7 K2 (ecb31049 shape: a supported claim about a method, then a fact that cuts against it, keyed That said). Moves: key outside the core 13; no obvious decoys; register near CB band 7 (glottochronology, vocabulary); the hardest decoy is Furthermore, for a reader who takes the blank sentence as more description of how the method works (its first clause does describe it). Decoys differ from ecb31049’s set. No In fact, Indeed or Actually decoy beside the concession key. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

band7.why: Same move and decoy relations as ecb31049 (That said after a supported claim about a method; unearned cause, specification, additive decoys), register 5.43 chars per word, key outside the core 13. The blank sentence opens with a description of the method ("it assumes ..."), so Furthermore pulls until the second clause. K2 sits near the 6/7 line, as the band-7 report says.

items.passage: Orchids are renowned for their partnerships with animal pollinators. Bees, moths, and other visitors collect sticky masses of pollen from one flower and inadvertently deposit them on another. ______ Holcoglossum amesianum, which blooms in southwestern China during the dry season, when such visitors are scarce, pollinates itself: its anther gradually rotates until the pollen is inserted into the flower’s own stigma.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first two sentences describe how orchids are known to be pollinated: they are “renowned for their partnerships with animal pollinators,” and visitors such as bees and moths carry pollen “from one flower” to “another.” The blank sentence names one orchid that does something different: Holcoglossum amesianum “pollinates itself.” “Alternatively” fits, since it signals that this orchid uses another means of pollination than the one just described.

A.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not reword the point about orchids and their animal pollinators; it describes an orchid that pollinates itself.

C.why_wrong: Holcoglossum amesianum is an orchid, but it is not an instance of an orchid relying on animal pollinators: it “pollinates itself.”

D.why_wrong: “Similarly” would mean this orchid also relies on visiting animals, but it blooms when “such visitors are scarce” and pollinates itself.

items.notes: Band-7 alternative (e225cf02 move: one named member of the group just described acts differently). Moves: same referent, new member (the orchid is one of the orchids of sentence 1, so For instance tempts); only instance or parallel decoys, no plain contrast word on offer; key outside the core 13. Sentence-initial blank and a species, not an individual animal, so the frame is not e225cf02’s. Plant: Holcoglossum amesianum (Liu et al. 2006, Nature), self-pollination by anther rotation without wind or insects. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

fixes: hardened: first sentence "Most orchids depend on animals for pollination" announced an exception before the blank; now "Orchids are renowned for their partnerships with animal pollinators," so For instance pulls on first read (e225cf02 gives no "most" cue); explanation and why_wrong A, C updated

band7.why: After the fix: e225cf02 move (a named member of the group acts differently), only instance, restatement and parallel decoys with no contrast word on offer, register about 5.5, key outside the core 13. The "Most orchids" cue that flagged the exception is gone, so For instance pulls until "pollinates itself."

items.passage: Tanzanian novelist Zawadi Mrema typically writes in Swahili, the language spoken in the coastal communities where her narratives unfold and where most of her readership resides. Her 2016 novel, ______ follows the staff of a Dar es Salaam call center that handles complaints from British customers, and it is written in English, the language the characters must speak with callers throughout their shifts.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes Mrema’s habit: she “typically writes in Swahili.” The blank sentence presents an exception to that habit: the novel “is written in English,” the language its characters “must speak with callers throughout their shifts.” “Nevertheless” fits, since it signals that this novel departs from what the previous sentence would lead a reader to expect.

B.why_wrong: The novel’s Tanzanian setting may look like more of Mrema’s usual work, but a novel “written in English” is not an example of her writing in Swahili; it is an exception to that habit.

C.why_wrong: Writing in Swahili, the language of her readers, is not a reason for writing a novel in English; the call-center setting is the reason.

D.why_wrong: “Likewise” would mean the 2016 novel follows the same practice as her other work, but it is in English, not Swahili.

items.notes: Band-7 C3 (fc95a352 move: a habit, then a one-off exception keyed Nevertheless, with no other adversative option, and the exception given a purpose). Moves: key not a contrast word; decoys example, cause, parallel. The blank is an interrupter after the subject (3.7 position) and the exception (written in English) comes late, after a call-center setting that reads like her usual coastal work (reviewer change), so the frame differs from fc95a352. Zawadi Mrema is an invented name (searched once 2026-10-20: no writer of that name). Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: The golomyanka, a translucent fish found only in Siberia’s Lake Baikal, reproduces in a manner that distinguishes it from nearly all other bony fishes. Rather than releasing eggs, the female gives birth to thousands of live larvae (newly hatched young). ______ more than 90 percent of bony fish species are egg layers, whose offspring develop and hatch outside the mother’s body.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence claims that the golomyanka reproduces in a manner that “distinguishes it from nearly all other bony fishes,” and the second explains that the female “gives birth to thousands of live larvae.” The blank sentence backs up the claim with a stronger fact: “more than 90 percent of bony fish species are egg layers.” Although its content differs from the golomyanka’s habit, it supports the point that the habit is rare, so “In fact” fits.

A.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean other fish lay eggs in spite of the golomyanka’s habit, but the egg-laying majority is exactly what makes that habit rare; the sentence supports the claim instead of conceding something against it.

B.why_wrong: The golomyanka’s habit does not cause other bony fish to lay eggs; the egg-laying majority is evidence of how unusual the habit is.

D.why_wrong: “Likewise” would mean other fish reproduce the way the golomyanka does, but they lay eggs while the golomyanka gives birth to live young.

items.notes: Band-7 M1 (surface contrast, supporting relation: the blank sentence describes fish that do the opposite of the golomyanka while proving its rarity). Moves: key outside the core 13; false-opposition decoy Nevertheless; no contrast word on offer (By contrast would also fit the content); the blank opens a sentence, and the claim is worded without the officials’ “outliers; indeed, the majority” skeleton. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

band7.why: M1 surface-contrast move of 47e238be and 00e0170f: the blank sentence describes egg layers, the opposite of the golomyanka, so Nevertheless pulls, while the relation is support for "distinguishes it from nearly all other bony fishes" two sentences back. Passes the surface-contrast proxy ("Rather than" before the blank); register 5.07 is below the 5.3 guide but the combined gate passes.

items.passage: In Finnish, primary stress invariably falls on the first syllable of a word, so listeners can identify word boundaries simply by attending to the emphasized syllables. Polish, ______ generally places stress on the penultimate (next-to-last) syllable, which means that the position of the stressed syllable shifts whenever grammatical endings lengthen a word.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text compares where two languages place word stress. In Finnish, stress “invariably falls on the first syllable,” while Polish “generally places stress on the penultimate (next-to-last) syllable.” Because the second language differs from the first, “by contrast” fits.

A.why_wrong: Polish is not an instance of Finnish stress; it puts the stress on a different syllable.

C.why_wrong: “Similarly” would mean Polish stresses words the way Finnish does, but Finnish stresses the first syllable and Polish the next-to-last.

D.why_wrong: Finnish stress patterns do not cause Polish to stress the next-to-last syllable; the two facts are about different languages.

items.notes: Interrupter after the second subject (2.6 shape), lowercase options. Subject: social science (linguistics). Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Because snow leopards are rare, wary, and spread across remote mountains, biologists in Mongolia estimate their numbers indirectly. They place motion-triggered cameras along ridgelines and identify individual cats by the distinctive pattern of rosettes on each animal’s coat. ______ they collect droppings and analyze the DNA they contain, which reveals each animal’s sex and its relatedness to others.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text describes how biologists “estimate their numbers indirectly.” The second sentence gives one method (cameras that let them identify cats by their rosettes), and the blank sentence gives a second, separate method (collecting droppings and analyzing “the DNA they contain”). “Additionally” fits, since it adds another item of the same kind.

A.why_wrong: “Regardless” would mean the DNA work ignores what the cameras show, but both methods serve the same survey.

B.why_wrong: “Instead” would mean the biologists collect droppings in place of using cameras, but they use both methods.

C.why_wrong: Setting cameras does not lead to collecting droppings; the two methods are independent.

items.notes: Two methods of one research effort (2.11 shape), option set not 2.11’s. Subject: natural science. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Japanese writer Ryūnosuke Akutagawa adapted several early stories from the Konjaku Monogatari, an anthology of tales compiled in the twelfth century. “The Nose” (1916) reimagines one of its narratives, concerning a Buddhist priest humiliated by his enormous nose. ______ “Yam Gruel” (1916) reimagines another, concerning a low-ranking official obsessed with eating his fill of a delicacy.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says Akutagawa “adapted several early stories from the Konjaku Monogatari.” “The Nose” “reimagines one of its narratives,” and “Yam Gruel” “reimagines another.” Since the second story does the same thing as the first, “Likewise” fits.

B.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean “Yam Gruel” reworks an old tale in spite of what “The Nose” does, but the two stories do the same thing.

C.why_wrong: “On the contrary” would mean the second story rejects the first, but both reimagine tales from the same anthology.

D.why_wrong: “The Nose” reworking a tale does not cause “Yam Gruel” to rework another one.

items.notes: Parallel case: a second work doing the same thing (2.7 shape). No addition decoy beside the similarity key; no example decoy (the passage names “several” stories, so For example could be argued). Subject: literature. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Analyzing the results of state exams taken by New York City high school students, a team of economists concluded that elevated temperatures can impair performance on high-stakes tests. ______ an individual student was considerably less likely to pass an exam administered on a 90°F day than one administered on a milder day.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence states the economists’ conclusion in general terms: “elevated temperatures can impair performance on high-stakes tests.” The blank sentence gives that finding exactly: a student “was considerably less likely to pass an exam administered on a 90°F day than one administered on a milder day.” “Specifically” fits, since it introduces the precise content of the general statement.

A.why_wrong: The blank sentence agrees with the conclusion that heat can impair performance; it does not contradict it.

B.why_wrong: The blank sentence is not a second finding; it spells out the one already stated.

D.why_wrong: “Meanwhile” would place the blank sentence’s fact alongside some other event, but it is the content of the economists’ conclusion.

items.notes: General finding, then its exact content. No causal decoy (a reader could argue For this reason: heat impairs performance, so students failed on hot days); no example or restatement decoy. Unnamed study, no figures beyond the 90°F threshold. Subject: social science (economics of education). Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Sharks are frequently described as needing to swim continuously in order to breathe, since forward motion forces oxygenated water across their gills. Nurse sharks, ______ can remain stationary on the seafloor for hours, relying on muscular contractions of the mouth and throat to pump water over their gills.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives a common belief: sharks need “to swim continuously in order to breathe.” The blank sentence describes sharks that break it: nurse sharks “can remain stationary on the seafloor for hours.” Since this fact contrasts with the belief, “however” fits.

A.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add nurse sharks as further support for the claim that sharks must keep swimming, but nurse sharks show the opposite.

B.why_wrong: Nurse sharks are not an example of sharks that must keep swimming; they rest without moving.

C.why_wrong: The belief that sharks must keep swimming does not cause nurse sharks to rest on the seafloor.

items.notes: Belief, then a case that breaks it, blank as an interrupter after the subject (2.16 shape). Subject: natural science. Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Until the early 1950s, motion pictures were printed on nitrate film, which burns easily and slowly decomposes unless stored in cool, dry conditions. Studios rarely kept their archives in such conditions, considering films that had finished their runs in theaters worthless. ______ many of the films made during the silent era no longer survive.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text explains that nitrate film “burns easily and slowly decomposes unless stored in cool, dry conditions,” and that studios “rarely kept their archives in such conditions.” The blank sentence gives the result: many silent films “no longer survive.” “Hence” fits, since it introduces a consequence of the facts before it.

B.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean the films were lost in spite of the conditions described, but those conditions explain the loss.

C.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not compare the silent films with anything in the earlier sentences; it states what happened to them.

D.why_wrong: “Meanwhile” would make the loss something happening alongside the studios’ storage habits, but it is the result of those habits.

items.notes: Reasons spread over two sentences, then the consequence keyed Hence (2.14 shape). Subject: arts and technology (film preservation). Facts from general knowledge, not web-checked (Transitions, user decision 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Women’s ski jumping made its Olympic debut at the 2014 Winter Games in Sochi, Russia, where Germany’s Carina Vogt claimed the inaugural gold medal in the competition. ______ the International Olympic Committee had rejected proposals to include the event, contending that the sport lacked sufficient numbers of elite female competitors to justify awarding Olympic medals.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes the event’s Olympic debut in 2014. The blank sentence describes what happened before that: the committee “had rejected proposals to include the event.” The past perfect “had rejected” shows that this came first, so “Previously” fits.

A.why_wrong: The 2014 debut did not cause the committee to reject the event; the rejection came before the debut.

C.why_wrong: The rejection is not an event similar to the debut; it is the earlier situation the debut ended.

D.why_wrong: The committee’s rejection is not an example of the event’s debut or of Vogt’s win.

items.passage: Public concerts became popular in the nineteenth century, and pianists increasingly played in large halls that held hundreds of listeners. In such spaces, the wooden-framed pianos of earlier decades sounded thin. ______ piano makers began building their instruments around cast-iron frames, which could withstand the enormous pull of thicker, tighter strings and so produce a considerably more powerful tone.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first two sentences describe a need: in large halls, “the wooden-framed pianos of earlier decades sounded thin.” The blank sentence describes how piano makers responded, with frames strong enough to hold strings that could “produce a considerably more powerful tone.” “Accordingly” fits, since it introduces an action taken in response to the situation just described.

A.why_wrong: Building iron frames is not one more fact about concert halls; it is the makers’ response to the problem the halls created.

B.why_wrong: The iron frames are not an example of pianos sounding thin in large halls; they were the solution to that problem.

C.why_wrong: “Regardless” would mean the makers acted without regard to the problem, but they acted because of it.

items.notes: Need, then the response of the people who could meet it, keyed Accordingly (2.17 relation; not a jury-and-award frame). Subject: arts and technology (instrument making).
